body:
Hi,

Thanks for reporting. If you can provide a PR it would expedite the fix!

I'm not sure how this should be fixed.    the description of the signatures suggests that the production of Index from reflection is wrong and this might be a SQLAlchemy bug. We do reflect "mssql_include", but if that's not considered part of `idx.columns` on the metadata side, it should also not be part of `idx.columns` on the reflection side.

also why does the phrase "mssql_include" not appear in test/dialect/mssql/test_reflection.py at all, yet I see logic that reflects this in mssql.get_indexes().   not sure how a feature is present there without a test
seems like it's tested in test_suite as PG has the same thing

ah, you are on SQLAlchemy 1.3.24.    this issue is fixed on the SQLAlhcemy side by https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/7382.   I will add a test to alembic but I can't reproduce in SQLAlchemy 1.4.
still trying to reproduce on older version just to make sure

OK confirmed this issue was fixed on the SQLAlchemy side by https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/4458.  reproduces earlier than that.

if you upgrade to 1.4 that will resolve.  otherwise, use an [include_object](https://alembic.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/api/runtime.html?highlight=include_object#alembic.runtime.environment.EnvironmentContext.configure.params.include_object) function to work around the issue within 1.3.

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **main** branch:

**add covering index tests; generalize autogen index tests** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/alembic/+/3709

Awesome, great finding @zzzeek! 
We once planned to upgrade to 1.4 but something stopped us from doing so (also related to mssql dialect), so we stayed on 1.3 for now. Thought this bug is related to the comparison in Alembic, but good to know it is already fixed in SQLAlchemy

Hi all,

I am facing the same issue with the following set

- Alembic 1.9
- SQLalchemy 1.4.36
- Psycop2 binary 2.9.5

The following model
```
import pytz
from datetime import datetime
from sqlalchemy import Boolean, Column, String, TIMESTAMP, Integer, ForeignKey, UniqueConstraint, Index
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import UUID
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker, scoped_session


SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URL = 'postgresql://test:password@localhost:5432/test'
engine = create_engine(SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URL)
Db_Session = scoped_session(
    sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine,)
)

Base = declarative_base()


class Entity(Base):

    __tablename__ = 'entities'

    id = Column(UUID(as_uuid=True), primary_key=True)
    owner_id = Column(UUID(as_uuid=True), nullable=True)
    is_active = Column(Boolean, default=True)
    is_deleted = Column(Boolean, default=False)
    created_at = Column(TIMESTAMP(timezone=True), default=datetime.now(tz=pytz.UTC))
    updated_at = Column(TIMESTAMP(timezone=True), default=datetime.now(tz=pytz.UTC), onupdate=datetime.now(tz=pytz.UTC))


```

It seems like every time I run a migration, Index are dropped and recreated. Do you guyz know how to help me solve this please

Thanks a lot

@louistwiice this is a separate issue so you should open a [discussion](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/alembic/discussions).   short answer, your model does not show any `Index` so if your actual database table has indexes in it, an autogenerate would show those being dropped .
